title: Turbo Boost Pressure Not Detected - Mechanical
shortDescription: Boost is not being produced as commanded.
fullDescription:
Ram 2500/3500 Cummins 6.7L uses a Holset VGT. P2262 indicates the turbo cannot make boost despite commanded VGT position.

Leading cause is sticky VGT vanes from soot. Cummins recommends Italian tune-up or actuator/turbo service.

fixSteps.title: Test boost system
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize charge air to 25 psi to find leaks.

fixSteps.title: Italian tune-up
fixSteps.instruction: Multiple WOT pulls in 3rd at operating temp can free vanes.

fixSteps.title: Replace VGT actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Holset HE351VE actuator, requires programming via Cummins Insite.

fixSteps.title: Turbo rebuild or replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If actuator OK and vanes locked, send Holset for rebuild.

whenToCallPro: Holset turbo service requires actuator initialization tools.

faq.a: Removing DPF reduces backpressure but is illegal.

title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
shortDescription: DEF rail pressure cannot reach commanded value.
fullDescription:
Ram 2500/3500 6.7L Cummins SCR system requires ~9 bar DEF pressure. P20E8 sets when low pressure is sustained.

Filter replacement and pump diaphragm wear are the usual culprits.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF filter
fixSteps.instruction: Mounted on supply module, replace cartridge and seals.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF pump module
fixSteps.instruction: Drain tank, swap pump module assembly.

faq.a: Cummins recommends DEF filter every 200k miles or as needed.

title: Reductant System Performance
shortDescription: SCR system performance metrics outside acceptable range.
fullDescription:
Ram-specific SCR performance code. Often follows P20EE-style faults. Indicates that DEF dosing is not producing adequate NOx reduction.

Check NOx sensors, DEF quality, and exhaust leaks.

fixSteps.title: Replace outlet NOx sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Most common failure; 22 mm socket access.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: V-band clamps and gaskets between turbo and SCR.

faq.a: After 200 mi countdown the truck will not start until repaired.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit Open
shortDescription: 5V reference voltage missing from one of the sensor groups.
fullDescription:
ECM provides 5V reference to multiple sensors. A short to ground on any one sensor pulls the bus down and triggers P0641 along with multiple sensor faults.

Isolate by disconnecting sensors one-by-one.

fixSteps.title: Note all simultaneous codes
fixSteps.instruction: All sensors on shared 5V will fault at once.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect sensors sequentially
fixSteps.instruction: Watch live data, when 5V returns the last disconnected sensor is shorted.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Common culprits: fuel rail pressure sensor, MAP, MAF.

whenToCallPro: ECM driver failure needs dealer service.

faq.a: No, ECM driver failure is rare; almost always a sensor or harness.

title: Fuel Delivery Error
shortDescription: Fuel delivery system not meeting target pressure or volume.
fullDescription:
Ram 6.7L Cummins uses Bosch CP3 (2007.5-2018) or CP4.2 (2019+). CP3 is robust; CP4.2 has disaster-failure risk.

Check filter for metal first.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel filters
fixSteps.instruction: Both engine and frame filters on 6.7L.

fixSteps.title: Cut filter for metal inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Metal shavings = CP4.2 disaster on 2019+ trucks.

whenToCallPro: CP4 disaster is dealer or specialist work.

faq.a: AirDog/FASS upgrades are popular for reliability and CP3 protection.

title: SKIM Key Not Programmed in PCM
shortDescription: Anti-theft module key signal not recognized.
fullDescription:
Ram trucks use SKIM (Sentry Key Immobilizer Module). P0633 sets after PCM replacement or key/SKIM communication loss.

Dealer programming is required to pair PCM and key.

fixSteps.title: Replace SKIM module
fixSteps.instruction: Behind dash, then re-pair to PCM.

faq.a: Mobile dealer-equipped locksmiths can program for less than dealer price.

title: Intake Air Heater System Performance
shortDescription: Grid heater not performing as commanded.
fullDescription:
Cummins uses an intake grid heater for cold start instead of glow plugs. P2609 sets when heater current draw is wrong, often from a corroded or melted bus bar - a known fire hazard.

Inspect bus bar urgently.

fixSteps.title: Inspect grid heater bus bar
fixSteps.instruction: URGENT: Look for melted/charred bus, replace immediately if damaged.

fixSteps.title: Test grid heater relay
fixSteps.instruction: Two relays under hood, swap with known good or test continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace grid heater
fixSteps.instruction: Located between intake horn and head, requires intake removal.

whenToCallPro: Only if intake removal is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Ram Cummins P2609 grid heater bus bar

faq.a: Yes, melted bus bars have caused engine fires; treat urgently.

title: Cooling Fan Rationality Check
shortDescription: Cooling fan not responding to control signals.
fullDescription:
6.7L Cummins uses an electronic viscous fan clutch with PWM control. P0483 sets when commanded vs actual fan speed disagrees.

Fan clutch wears out; replace as a unit.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pigtail at fan
fixSteps.instruction: Look for melted or chafed wires.

fixSteps.title: Test PWM signal at fan
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe and check duty cycle changes with command.

faq.a: Electronically controlled viscous clutch - hybrid of both.

title: Turbocharger Underboost
fullDescription:
Generic underboost code on 6.7L Cummins. Common from sticky Holset VGT, charge air leaks, or restricted exhaust (clogged DPF).

Log desired vs actual boost to confirm.

fixSteps.title: Pressure-test charge air
fixSteps.instruction: 25 psi shop air, check for hisses.

fixSteps.title: DPF backpressure check
fixSteps.instruction: wiTECH live data: backpressure should be reasonable at idle.

fixSteps.title: VGT actuator test
fixSteps.instruction: Sweep 0-100 percent and watch boost change.

whenToCallPro: Holset turbo work needs special tools.

faq.a: Yes, charge air boots typically fail in this range.

title: ECM/PCM Internal Performance Failure
fullDescription:
Internal ECM fault. Often follows water intrusion or aftermarket tuner-related corruption.

Return to stock tune first; if persists, ECM replacement and dealer programming.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ECM enclosure for water
fixSteps.instruction: Located inside fender, look for moisture or corrosion.

whenToCallPro: ECM programming is dealer or qualified locksmith only.

faq.a: Yes, removing tuner before service is critical.
